nodes.content: Infer calibrated, multimodal 3D human motion from monocular video despite occlusion and previously unseen camera viewpoints.
requirements: Attain 87–93% empirical coverage for nominal 90% motion regions under occlusion and unseen viewpoints.
Reduce prediction-region volume by 20% versus a calibrated unimodal predictor at matched coverage.

nodes.content: Train visibility-aware, camera-equivariant motion diffusion; conformally calibrate compact unions of 3D trajectory tubes using held-out camera viewpoints.
Which visibility-weighted nonconformity score calibrates unions of motion tubes across held-out viewpoints without filling gaps between modes?
A minimum-over-modes visibility-normalized residual, calibrated by occlusion and camera-angle strata, maintains 87–93% coverage with 20% less volume than unimodal regions.
Compare pooled versus occlusion-and-viewpoint-stratified minimum-over-modes residual calibration on held-out-camera Human3.6M, measuring coverage and matched-coverage union volume.
Run five-seed Human3.6M leave-one-camera-out trials with 40% joint occlusion; compare pooled/stratified coverage and matched-coverage volume against a unimodal baseline.
Across five held-out-camera Human3.6M seeds with 40% occlusion, stratified tubes covered 84% (nominal 90%); matched-coverage volume fell 12% versus unimodal.
A camera-shift-weighted, visibility-normalized mode-minimum residual with mode pruning will achieve 87–93% coverage and ≥20% matched-coverage volume reduction versus unimodal.
Run Human3.6M leave-one-camera-out trials at 40% occlusion; evaluate shift-weighted calibration and mode pruning for coverage and matched-coverage volume versus unimodal.
On Human3.6M held-out-camera trials with 40% occlusion, shift-weighted pruned tubes achieved 89% coverage and 23% lower matched-coverage volume than unimodal.
Adopt shift-weighted, mode-pruned calibration: unlike the earlier 84% coverage result, it achieves 89% coverage and 23% lower matched-coverage volume.
Using adopted shift-weighted, pruned tubes, compare pooled versus occlusion-and-viewpoint-stratified calibration on held-out-camera Human3.6M for coverage and matched-coverage volume.
Human3.6M calibration report with per-camera coverage, matched-coverage volume, and pooled-versus-stratified comparisons for adopted shift-weighted, pruned tubes.
How can camera-equivariant diffusion preserve distinct 3D motion modes when occlusion hides limbs and the test camera is unseen?
Ablate equivariant conditioning and visibility masks in diffusion on held-out-camera Human3.6M at 40% occlusion; measure oracle MPJPE and diversity.
On held-out-camera Human3.6M, masks plus equivariance lowered oracle MPJPE from 58 to 45 mm versus ablation, retaining 48-mm pairwise diversity.
Stress-test calibrated diffusion on 3DPW held-out azimuth bins with limb occlusion; measure mode recall, coverage, and matched-coverage volume.
On 3DPW unseen-azimuth limb occlusion, tubes covered 81% (nominal 90%) and reduced matched-coverage volume only 9% versus unimodal.
Use n13’s per-camera calibration report to predict 3DPW azimuth failures; test predictions against occluded-mode recall and empirical coverage.
Report-flagged rear-oblique 3DPW bins showed 73% coverage and 54% occluded-mode recall, versus 88% and 76% elsewhere.
Retain masked equivariant diffusion, but defer cross-dataset deployment; prioritize rear-oblique mode recovery and recalibration after 3DPW failures.
Add render-and-compare camera-latent inference and rear-oblique occlusion augmentation to diffusion; recalibrate recovered modes on shifted validation viewpoints.
Can render-and-compare camera inference recover rear-oblique occluded modes without enlarging calibrated trajectory unions?
Camera-latent refinement and augmentation raise rear-oblique mode recall above 70%, yielding 87–93% 3DPW coverage and ≥20% smaller regions versus unimodal.
Ablate camera-latent refinement and rear-oblique augmentation on occluded 3DPW; measure mode recall, recalibrated coverage, and matched-coverage volume versus unimodal.
On occluded 3DPW rear-oblique bins, mode recall reached 74%; recalibrated coverage was 89%, with 22% less volume than matched-coverage unimodal.
Adopt camera-latent refinement with rear-oblique augmentation and shifted-view calibration; 3DPW rear-oblique coverage reached 89% with 22% volume reduction.
Learn a camera-marginalized, action-conditioned normalizing flow with occlusion-aware particle smoothing; calibrate disconnected highest-density trajectory sets.
Does camera marginalization preserve rare action-dependent trajectory modes under occlusion while keeping highest-density sets compact on unseen viewpoints?
Particle-smoothed camera-marginalized flow retains ≥75% rare-action mode recall on occluded unseen-view 3DPW; regions achieve 87–93% coverage, ≥20% smaller than unimodal.
Run rare-action 3DPW unseen-azimuth occlusion trials; measure flow mode recall, 90% region coverage, and matched-coverage volume versus unimodal.
On rare-action occluded 3DPW unseen azimuths, flow retained 61% mode recall and 85% coverage; matched-coverage volume decreased 14% versus unimodal.
Rare-action-stratified particles and camera-conditioned proposals yield ≥75% mode recall, 87–93% coverage, and ≥20% smaller regions than unimodal.
Ablate stratified particles and camera-conditioned proposals in camera-marginalized 3DPW flow; measure occluded unseen-view mode recall, coverage, and matched-coverage volume.
On occluded unseen-view 3DPW, stratified flow achieved 78% rare-action mode recall, 90% coverage, and 21% lower matched-coverage volume versus unimodal.
Test stratified flow on disjoint 3DPW subjects and unseen azimuths with 60% occlusion; measure rare-action recall, coverage, and matched-coverage volume.
On disjoint-subject 3DPW with unseen azimuths and 60% occlusion: 68% rare-action recall, 83% coverage, 13% smaller matched-coverage regions versus unimodal.
Subject-invariant kinematic priors and occlusion-adaptive particles restore ≥75% rare-action recall, 87–93% coverage, and ≥20% volume reduction under 60% occlusion.
Ablate invariant priors and adaptive particle counts on disjoint-subject 3DPW at 60% occlusion; measure recall, coverage, matched-coverage volume.
On disjoint-subject 3DPW at 60% occlusion, invariant-prior adaptive flow achieved 76% rare-action recall, 89% coverage, 22% lower matched-coverage volume.
Validate n40’s invariant-prior adaptive-flow checkpoint on new-subject, unseen-azimuth 3DPW at 60% occlusion; measure rare-action recall, coverage, matched-coverage volume.
On new-subject, unseen-azimuth 3DPW at 60% occlusion, rare-action recall fell to 70%, coverage to 85%, volume reduction to 16%.
Test-time bone-length adaptation of camera-marginalized particles restores ≥75% rare-action recall, 87–93% coverage, and ≥20% matched-coverage volume reduction.
Compare bone-length-adapted versus unadapted invariant-prior adaptive flows on new-subject unseen-azimuth 3DPW (60% occlusion); measure recall, coverage, matched-coverage volume.
Disjoint-subject unseen-azimuth controls replicated 76% recall, 89% coverage, 22% matched-coverage volume reduction; bone-adapted new-subject cases achieved 72%, 86%, 18%.
Stratify new-subject 3DPW at 60% occlusion by unseen azimuth and bone-length mismatch; measure adapted-flow rare-mode recall, coverage, and volume.
On unseen-azimuth 3DPW at 60% occlusion, adapted flow achieved 77% rare-action recall, 89% coverage, 21% volume reduction for ≤5%-mismatch subjects.
Use bone-adapted flow only for ≤5%-mismatch subjects (89% coverage, 21% volume reduction); defer broader deployment after 86%/18% overall.
Combine subject-shape-marginalized inverse-kinematics ensembles with occlusion-aware conformal calibration to retain compact motion modes across unseen viewpoints.
Can shape-marginalized inverse kinematics recover occluded motion modes for >5%-mismatch subjects without inflating unseen-view prediction regions?
Under >5% shape mismatch and 60% occlusion, shape-marginalized IK achieves ≥75% rare-mode recall, 87–93% coverage, ≥20% smaller regions than unimodal.
Train shape-marginalized IK ensembles, calibrate occlusion-stratified trajectory unions, then test >5%-mismatch 3DPW subjects at unseen azimuths.
Evaluate calibrated shape-marginalized IK on >5%-mismatch 3DPW subjects with unseen azimuths and 60% occlusion; compare rare-mode recall and matched-coverage volume.
On >5%-mismatch 3DPW unseen-azimuths at 60% occlusion, shape-marginalized IK: 77% rare-mode recall, 89% coverage, 22% less matched-coverage volume versus unimodal.
Using n54’s IK checkpoint, test disjoint >5%-mismatch 3DPW subjects at unseen azimuths and 60% occlusion for coverage, recall, matched-coverage volume.
Disjoint-subject 3DPW validation table listing rare-mode recall, nominal-90% coverage, and matched-coverage volume by bone-length mismatch and azimuth.
Audit n56’s mismatch-by-azimuth table; replicate worst-bin IK trials at 60% occlusion against unimodal coverage and matched-coverage volume.
Worst-bin high-mismatch unseen-azimuth 3DPW replication at 60% occlusion: 87% coverage, 75% rare-mode recall, 20% lower matched-coverage volume versus unimodal.
Train camera-invariant bidirectional motion bridges with foot-contact constraints to span occluded intervals; calibrate disconnected 3D trajectory regions.
Do foot-contact constraints preserve multiple plausible trajectories across long occlusions without overconstraining motion from unseen camera angles?
Contact-conditioned bridges achieve 87–93% coverage and ≥20% lower matched-coverage volume than unimodal on unseen-view 3DPW with ≥1-second occlusions.
Compare contact-conditioned bridges with contact-free bridges and calibrated unimodal predictors on unseen-view 3DPW ≥1-second occlusions; measure coverage and matched-coverage volume.
On unseen-view 3DPW ≥1-second occlusions, contact-conditioned bridges covered 82% (nominal 90%) and reduced matched-coverage volume 11% versus unimodal.
Stratify unseen-view 3DPW long-occlusion trials by contact-label confidence; compare bridge mode recall, coverage, and matched-coverage volume against contact-free bridges.
On unseen-view 3DPW ≥1-second occlusions with ≥0.9 contact confidence, bridges achieved 90% coverage and 22% lower matched-coverage volume versus unimodal.
Confidence-gated bridges applying contact constraints only above 0.9 confidence achieve 87–93% coverage and ≥20% volume reduction across long occlusions.
Run confidence-gated versus always-on contact bridges across unseen-view 3DPW ≥1-second occlusions; measure nominal-90% coverage and matched-coverage volume.
Across unseen-view 3DPW ≥1-second occlusions, confidence-gated bridges achieved 89% coverage and 21% less matched-coverage volume than unimodal.
Freeze n68’s validated 0.9-confidence gate; evaluate on disjoint-subject unseen-view 3DPW ≥1-second occlusions for coverage and matched-coverage volume.
On disjoint-subject unseen-view 3DPW ≥1-second occlusions, frozen-gate bridges covered 84% and reduced matched-coverage volume 15% versus unimodal.
Subject-adaptive confidence thresholds from visible foot-ground reprojection restore 87–93% coverage and ≥20% matched-coverage volume reduction on disjoint-subject unseen-view long occlusions.
Revisit n70’s disjoint-subject failures; estimate subject-specific contact gates from visible foot-ground reprojection, then compare coverage and volume against frozen gates.
On disjoint-subject unseen-view 3DPW ≥1-second occlusions, adaptive gates reached 86% coverage and 18% volume reduction versus unimodal.
Stratify adaptive-gate disjoint-subject 3DPW long occlusions by visible foot-ground reprojection error; measure mode recall, coverage, matched-coverage volume.
At ≤4-pixel foot-ground reprojection error, adaptive gates achieved 89% coverage and 21% lower matched-coverage volume on disjoint-subject unseen-view 3DPW.
Restrict adaptive contact gating to ≤4-pixel reprojection error; elsewhere use contact-free bridges to maintain 87–93% coverage and ≥20% volume reduction.
Using n73’s deficits and n75’s ≤4-pixel stratum, test adaptive-gated/contact-free switching on disjoint-subject unseen-view 3DPW; measure coverage and matched-coverage volume.
On disjoint-subject unseen-view 3DPW ≥1-second occlusions, switched bridges attained 88% coverage and 20% lower matched-coverage volume versus unimodal.
Adopt ≤4-pixel adaptive-contact/contact-free switching: it restores 88% coverage and 20% volume reduction versus unimodal, outperforming adaptive gating alone.
Using the adopted ≤4-pixel switch, stratify long-occlusion 3DPW by azimuth; assess mode recall and contact violations, then recalibrate failing bins.
Stratify adopted ≤4-pixel-switch 3DPW long occlusions by unseen azimuth; measure mode recall, contact violations, coverage, and matched-coverage volume versus unimodal.
3DPW azimuth-stratified audit table reporting switched-bridge mode recall, contact violations, nominal-90% coverage, and matched-coverage volume versus unimodal.

Reduce prediction-region volume by 20% versus a calibrated unimodal predictor at matched coverage.
